question: Can fathers take paid leave when their baby is born?
raw:
ANSWER: Yes, a married male employee shall be entitled to a paid paternity leave at his ordinary rate of pay for a period of seven consecutive days in respect of each confinement.

QUOTE: (1) Subject to subsection (3), a married male employee shall be entitled to a paid paternity leave at his ordinary rate of pay for a period of seven consecutive days in respect of each confinement.
quote: (1) Subject to subsection (3), a married male employee shall be entitled to a paid paternity leave at his ordinary rate of pay for a period of seven consecutive days in respect of each confinement.
answer: Yes, a married male employee shall be entitled to a paid paternity leave at his ordinary rate of pay for a period of seven consecutive days in respect of each confinement. [s60FA]

question: How much notice must I give if I want to resign?

answer: The length of the notice shall be the same for both employer and employee and shall be determined by a provision made in writing for such notice in the terms of the contract of service, or, in the absence of such provision in writing, shall not be less than four weeks’ notice if the employee has been so employed for less than two years on the date on which the notice is given. question: Does my employer have to give me a day off every week?
raw:
ANSWER: No, your employer does not have to give you a day off every week. The employer is allowed to grant the rest day for each week on any day of the month in which the rest days fall, subject to the Director General's approval.

QUOTE: Notwithstanding subsection (1) and interpretation of the expression “day” in subsection 2(1), in the case of an employee engaged in shift work any continuous period of not less than thirty hours shall constitute a rest day.
quote: Notwithstanding subsection (1) and interpretation of the expression “day” in subsection 2(1), in the case of an employee engaged in shift work any continuous period of not less than thirty hours shall constitute a rest day.
answer: No, your employer does not have to give you a day off every week. The employer is allowed to grant the rest day for each week on any day of the month in which the rest days fall, subject to the Director General's approval. [s59]

question: Can my boss make me work on my weekly rest day and do I get paid extra?
raw:

QUOTE: (1) Except as provided in subsection 60A(2), no employee shall be compelled to work on a rest day unless he is engaged in work which by reason of its nature requires to be carried on continuously or continually by two or more shifts:

question: How many public holidays does my employer have to give me each year?
raw:
ANSWER: The employer shall exhibit conspicuously at the place of employment before the commencement of each calendar year a notice specifying the remaining six gazetted public holidays provided for in paragraph (1) (a) in respect of which his employees shall be entitled to paid holidays under paragraph (1) (a).

QUOTE: (1) Every employee shall be entitled to a paid holiday at his ordinary rate of pay on the following days in any one calendar year: (a) on eleven of the gazetted public holidays, five of which shall be— (i) the National Day; (ii) the Birthday of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong; (iii) the Birthday of the Ruler or the Yang di-Pertua Negeri, as the case may be, of the State in which the employee wholly or mainly works under his contract of service, or the Federal Territory Day, if the employee wholly or mainly works in the Federal Territory; (iv) the Workers’ Day; and (v) Malaysia Day;

question: What happens to my annual leave if I fall sick during it?
raw:
ANSWER: If an employee who is on paid annual leave becomes entitled to sick leave or maternity leave while on such annual leave, the employee shall be granted the sick leave or the maternity leave, as the case may be, and the annual leave shall be deemed to have not been taken in respect of the days for which sick leave or maternity leave is so granted.
QUOTE: (b) Where an employee who is on paid annual leave becomes entitled to sick leave or maternity leave while on such annual leave, the employee shall be granted the sick leave or the maternity leave, as the case may be, and the annual leave shall be deemed to have not been taken in respect of the days for which sick leave or maternity leave is so granted.

question: Can I be fired for being absent from work without telling my employer?
raw:
ANSWER: Yes, you can be deemed to have broken your contract of service with your employer if you have been continuously absent from work for more than two consecutive working days without prior leave from your employer.

QUOTE: An employee shall be deemed to have broken his contract of service with the employer if he has been continuously absent from work for more than two consecutive working days without prior leave from his employer, unless he has a reasonable excuse for such absence and has informed or attempted to inform his employer of such excuse prior to or at the earliest opportunity during such absence.
quote: An employee shall be deemed to have broken his contract of service with the employer if he has been continuously absent from work for more than two consecutive working days without prior leave from his employer, unless he has a reasonable excuse for such absence and has informed or attempted to inform his employer of such excuse prior to or at the earliest opportunity during such absence.
answer: Yes, you can be deemed to have broken your contract of service with your employer if you have been continuously absent from work for more than two consecutive working days without prior leave from your employer. [s15]

question: What is the longest a shift worker can be made to work?
raw:
ANSWER: The longest a shift worker can be made to work is forty-five hours in any one week, but the average number of hours worked over any period of three weeks shall not exceed forty-five per week.

QUOTE: (1) Notwithstanding paragraphs 60 a(1)(b), (c) and (d), but subject to paragraph (1) (a) thereof, an employee who is engaged under his contract of service in shift work may be required by his employer to work more than eight hours in any one day or more than forty-five hours in any one week but the average number of hours worked over any period of three weeks, or over any period exceeding three weeks as may be approved by the Director General, shall not exceed forty-five per week.
quote: (1) Notwithstanding paragraphs 60 a(1)(b), (c) and (d), but subject to paragraph (1) (a) thereof, an employee who is engaged under his contract of service in shift work may be required by his employer to work more than eight hours in any one day or more than forty-five hours in any one week but the average number of hours worked over any period of three weeks, or over any period exceeding three weeks as may be approved by the Director General, shall not exceed forty-five per week.
answer: The longest a shift worker can be made to work is forty-five hours in any one week, but the average number of hours worked over any period of three weeks shall not exceed forty-five per week. [s60C]

question: What does the law mean by wages?
raw:
ANSWER: Wages means the remuneration payable to an employee for his work, including any allowance or benefit, and includes any payment made to an employee in lieu of wages, but does not include any payment made to an employee in respect of any approved incentive payment scheme.
